[WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p60#2/r2] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | The related wording in 30:60 means do not let those without certainty drive you into ignorance or incline you toward them. | mentions 30:60
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p60#2/r3] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · مقاتل والفراء | reports | Muqatil and al-Farra gloss the verb as provoking the Egyptians; al-Wahidi explains that Pharaoh unsettled them and led them into ignorance through deceit and the claim that he showed them only what he saw. | mentions 40:29
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p60#2/r4] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | rejects | Al-Wahidi rejects interpreting the verb as merely finding the people foolish: their obedience requires Pharaoh to have urged them to something, and that reading needs an impermissible omitted step, unlike the sense of agitating them.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p60#2/r5] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن عباس ومقاتل | reports | Ibn Abbas and Muqatil say the people obeyed Pharaoh by rejecting Moses; Pharaoh induced ignorance, and they accepted his claim and denied Moses.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p61/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | The people Moses had led were disobedient to God.
[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:54-57/r1] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | Pharaoh made his Coptic people out to be ignorant, and they obeyed him; they were a sinful people.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p217#2/r4] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | Pharaoh made his Egyptian people seem foolish, finding them ignorant.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p217#2/r5] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | reports | Another gloss is that Pharaoh led them into frivolity and ignorance, removing them from sound judgment.

[TABRISI:43:51-54/r12] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | Pharaoh’s people were outside obedience to God.

[QURTUBI-FULL:43:54/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The verb can mean that joy unsettles someone or that someone induces another to act foolishly; the related verse warns against being unsettled by unbelievers. | mentions 30:60
[QURTUBI-FULL:43:54/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | reports | Another interpretation is that Pharaoh provoked his people with speech, and they obeyed him by accepting disbelief.
[QURTUBI-FULL:43:54/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | reports | A further view says he found them intellectually weak; this alone cannot explain their obedience, so an unstated step must be supplied: he called them to error and they obeyed.
[QURTUBI-FULL:43:54/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | reports | Another view takes the phrase as Pharaoh overpowering his people until they followed him; استخف به means to insult someone.
[QURTUBI-FULL:43:54/r6] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | They were a people who had departed from obedience to God.

[BAYDAWI-FULL:43:54-56/r2] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | They obeyed Pharaoh in what he ordered because they were a wicked people.

[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p383/r2] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | reports | Another view says Pharaoh made them pliant and easily led, and their wickedness made them obey him.

[BIQAI-FULL:v7p37/r8] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Their obedience meant acknowledging Pharaoh's kingship and grandeur, affirming his lordship, and rejecting Moses' command.
[BIQAI-FULL:v7p37/r9] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Moses had answered every threat and request with signs that surpassed bracelets and angels, so the Egyptians had no reason to obey Pharaoh except affinity in evil character.
[DURR-FULL:v7p383/r9] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · عكرمة | reports | Ikrimah says Pharaoh did not let out anyone older than forty or younger than twenty, exemplifying how he made his people comply in pursuing Moses.

[BURSEVI:v8p292#2/r2] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | They rushed to obey Pharaoh because they were a wicked people outside God’s obedience and sound reason, trusting transient wealth and rank and looking down on Moses.

[BURSEVI:v8p292#2/r4] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | An enemy never truly submits; do not trust compelled obedience, since, given an opening, the enemy would cut a hand off instead of kissing it.
[BURSEVI:v8p292/r3] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Pharaoh’s deception made his people intellectually lightweight and quick to obey; the requested lightness concerns their judgment, not bodily speed, or means he found their minds credulous.
[BURSEVI:v8p292/r4] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · الراغب | reports | Al-Raghib allows that Pharaoh made them hasten to follow him or found them lightweight in body and resolve.
[BURSEVI:v8p292/r5] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · القاموس | reports | Al-Qamus gives استخفه as the opposite of making someone weighty, or as leading someone into ignorance and fickleness and away from sound judgment.

[IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p233/r3] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Lightness is a metaphor for shifting from reflection and hesitation to swift compliance, as an object becomes light after being heavy.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p233/r4] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The phrase also means Pharaoh made them intellectually frivolous: after inwardly crediting Moses because of his signs, they quickly accepted Pharaoh's claims.

[IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p233/r6] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The added sīn and tāʾ intensify أخف, as in the verse about Satan causing a slip and the Arabic phrase about provoking a sensible person's anger. | mentions 3:155

[IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p233/r9] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Fāsiqīn here means unbelievers, as the Qur'an describes these people in the verse about the abode of the wicked. | mentions 7:145
[TABATABAI:43:54-56/r1] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | Pharaoh made his people’s minds and judgment foolish, and so they obeyed him.
[TABATABAI:43:54-56/r2] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | The people are described as transgressors and sinners.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p170/r6] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | Moses and Jesus both called people to monotheism; Pharaoh and his chiefs rejected Moses' successive signs for the same arrogant reason as Quraysh and met their deserved fate, which Quraysh will also face.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | Every part of Sūrah al-Zukhruf relates deeply to its central theme, and the whole sūrah forms a harmonious unit from beginning to end.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p200/r4] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | The verb istakhafa is opposite to istathqala: Pharaoh treated his people as simpletons, lured them, and they followed foolishly.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p200/r5] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | Their disobedience and lack of faith left them spiritually insignificant and easy for Satan to lead; a person gains weight through relationship with God.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:45/r1] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | The account of Moses’ confrontation with Pharaoh and his people supplies historical lessons within the Prophet’s call and struggle for tawhid.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:45/r2] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | Unbelievers retain a deep belief in God that worldly incentives and suggestions bury; disasters sent in mercy revive it, but they return to denial when hardship passes.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:45/r3] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | Tawhid is every prophet’s shared message: scripture and its remnants show that God never permitted worship of another being, as Moses’ struggle also proves.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:45/r4] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | The verb istikhfaf can mean hastening, deceiving, exploiting ignorance, belittling people for weakness, or directing them as one wishes.
